title: Why does LZ's likelihood still give 2.7σ to spectra with tens of low-energy events? A joint low/high-energy reassessment
question: How much 5.4-55 keV signal does LZ's unbinned likelihood tolerate per operator, why do N_lo ~ 30 spectra keep ~2.7 sigma, what happens when the 2024 low-energy null is imposed explicitly (N_max = 3-20), and which operators keep >= 3 sigma / carry the posterior mass?
headline_result: A few-bin likelihood from the digitised Fig. 5 S1c<250 phd panel reproduces Tables S6/S7 (rms 0.21 sigma; O4 2.70 vs 2.7, O11s 1.90 vs 1.7, O1s 0.48 vs 0.0): the profile fit tolerates only 1.6-2.2 low-energy events by shrinking the 248 keV signal to s_hat = 0.06 events (P(event) = 5.5%), so local Z falls only logarithmically with N_lo (below 2 sigma at N_lo ~ 160) and an explicit 2024 null with N_max = 3 shifts it by <= 0.16 sigma, whereas Bayes factors collapse from 45 (L10) to 1.6 (O4) and 1.0 (O1, O11s), leaving 87% of the posterior mass in N_lo <= 5 operators
model_or_mechanism: few-bin extended Poisson likelihood (Fig. 5 NR-band projection bins + 125-200 keV bin + 200-270 keV bin) with profiled ER-leakage scale; closed-form profile maximum b_L u^2 = 1+u; Gaussian 2024 constraint; P001 single-event Bayes factor with marginal low-energy likelihood
stance: statistical reassessment (weakens the case for O1/O4/O7/O11/O12-type elastic interactions; strengthens the relative case for q^2-suppressed spin operators and L10)
